cards.label: Woven Wonders
cards.challenge: Why do people weave patterns? What can cloth tell us?

video.title: Climbing a giant net at a science museum

cards.printAnswer: Patterns can mean stories, families, or just play. Cloth shows what people had and what they cared about.

cards.label: Imaginarium
cards.challenge: What is imagination for? Could you invent a new animal?

video.title: A glowing sand table at the Exploratorium

cards.printAnswer: Imagination lets us try ideas before they are real. Yes — mix parts and tell how your animal lives.

cards.label: Hands-on Lab
cards.challenge: Why do scientists do tests? What would you try?
cards.printAnswer: A test is how we check a guess. Pick one question and change just one thing.

cards.label: Creative Makery
cards.challenge: Why do makers try, fail, and try again?

video.title: Making in the Exploratorium Tinkering Studio

cards.printAnswer: Most first tries do not work. Each fail shows what to change next.

cards.label: Art Lab
cards.challenge: Why do colors mix the way they do?
cards.printAnswer: Paints mix by subtracting light; screens mix by adding light. Red and blue do not make the same thing both ways.

cards.label: Free Explore
cards.challenge: What makes you curious? What would you look up?
cards.printAnswer: Curious is your brain asking why. Write the question and hunt for one true clue.

cards.label: Space Shuttle
cards.challenge: Why do rockets need such a big boost? Where does the crew sit?
cards.printAnswer: Leaving Earth takes a huge push against gravity. The crew sits in a small cabin at the top.

cards.label: Astronaut Life
cards.challenge: Why is food weird in space? What would you pack?

video.title: Looking back at Earth from the cupola

cards.printAnswer: There is no down, so crumbs float. Pack food that sticks together and will not make a mess.

cards.label: Planet Hall
cards.challenge: Why do planets look different? Which would you visit, and why?
cards.printAnswer: Each planet is a different mix of rock, gas, heat, and distance from the sun. Pick one and say what you would go see.

cards.label: Rockets
cards.challenge: How does a rocket leave Earth? Why so tall?
cards.printAnswer: Hot gas blasts down so the rocket goes up. It is tall because it stacks fuel under the crew.
